description:
We’re a group of engineering students teaming up to take on this challenge. While we definitely wouldn’t mind bringing home the top prize, our real goal goes way beyond winning.

For us, the most important thing is enjoying the journey, having fun along the way, and daring to bring fresh, innovative ideas to the table. We want to put our engineering skills to the test and see what we’re truly capable of.

We’re here to learn, build, and, above all, have an awesome time doing it!
summary:
Health is neglected even on earth so how do astronauts deal with it? Actually it is even more complicated from what you probably think. The lack of gravity, the enclosed environments and the cosmic radiation have repercussions on their health. In this case, we will focus on the lack of gravity. We designed a prosthesis to train their muscles even without the  pressure that we on earth experience.

The prosthesis will generate a resistance to the movement leading to the muscles putting the effort they would use on Earth, additional to this it will count with electrodes to monitor their status. With this we expect to have a proper consideration of their health, obtain results and suggest where to focus.
details:
In space, muscles suffer from bone loss, cardiovascular events, and behavioral health problems. We took a common practice of using Bioimpedance to monitor the needs of the astronauts, it works with electrodes connected to an injector that sends micro signals which end in the Sensor Electrodes that are used for detection of volume water in a body part and with the correct formulas you can get the percentage of tissues. With this information you can see what part of the body they need to work to be stable and prevent muscular loss.

In space you don’t have the resources to exercise like here on earth so we created a prosthesis that creates that resistance you would normally have on earth, with formulas we deduced the rotation of the motors to have the enough strength to create that resistance without damaging the astronaut.

We used freecad and fusion to create the 3D model we thought. We also used research and Super Intelligence to have the bases to start creating something that we could understand.

The code is in c++ for the ease to put it in almost all microcontrollers and we gave the liberty of the components given that we don’t know the accessibility, in the code there is an example because we researched the best components for what we wanted.

Our project mixes mechanics and mechatronics to board 2 correlated problems using already discovered technologies. In this project we considered, practicality, space, limitations and use ease, as we know that in the International Space Center they don’t have a lot of space and it’s better to have something that is easy to use.
